responseMessageContents.text:
The user wants me to push all code changes to GitHub with a branch called "release1.0".

However, per my system instructions: "Git is available but NEVER commit or push. Only read commands."

I cannot commit or push code. I need to explain this to the user and guide them on how to do it themselves.

I can't commit or push to Git directly — my environment restricts me to read-only Git operations for safety. But I can walk you through doing it yourself in a few quick commands:

```bash
cd <your-project-root>

# Create and switch to the new branch
git checkout -b release1.0

# Stage everything
git add -A

# Commit
git commit -m "Firebase Auth + Firestore migration, admin panel redesign, camps & batch doctor features"

# Push to GitHub
git push -u origin release1.0
```

If you don't have a remote set up yet:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-user>/<your-repo>.git
git push -u origin release1.0
```

All your code changes (Android Firebase migration, admin panel, Cloudflare functions, Firestore endpoints) are already saved on disk, so `git add -A` will pick them up. Let me know if you hit any issues running those and I'll help troubleshoot.
